data.description:
## This is the LAST child. Do not start it early.

Flipping `sweep (windows)` to voting before S1–S9 are green would redden every change with
failures unrelated to the change under review. That is not a stricter gate; it is the destruction of
the `Verified` signal, and it is the precise failure mode **ADR 0114** was written to prevent after
incident `90c7-c465-4037-42d5` — where a check wired straight into the required aggregate failed on
every change, including the changes that would have repaired it, and only a human force-submit broke
the lock.

## Blocked by every other child

S1 (`friendless-alabaster-cub`), S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, and S10 must all be closed first.

## The two-step rollout ADR 0114 mandates

1. **Advisory green first.** With S1–S9 landed, `sweep (windows)` must produce at least one
   **passing run on `main`, independent of the required `Verified` hot path** — i.e. still
   non-voting, still outside `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s aggregate `needs`. Record that run's id.
2. **Promotion, as a separate change.** Only then may a later change remove
   `continue-on-error: true`, widen the `if:` condition beyond `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`, and
   wire the job into the required aggregate in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`. The
   promotion change's description must cite the run id from step 1 — ADR 0114 makes that citation a
   review requirement, not a courtesy.

## A cost decision this story must make explicitly

`sweep (windows)` took **662.75s (11:02)** for the default suite in job `100874330553`. Windows
runners are the slowest and most expensive in the matrix. Entering the `Verified` hot path adds that
to every change's critical path.

Decide deliberately between: the full default suite on Windows, or a **reduced `platform_compat`
subset** as the gate with the full suite left on the schedule — which is exactly the shape already
used for macOS (`sweep (macos, full suite)` is the scheduled full run; the gate takes the reduced
`platform_compat` selection, story `8d36`). Precedent favours the reduced subset. State the choice
and its reasoning in the promotion change.

## Proving command

Step 1 (advisory green):
```
gh workflow run test.yml --ref main
gh run watch --exit-status      # sweep (windows): 0 failed, 0 errors, job conclusion success
```
Step 2 (promotion landed):
```
grep -n "continue-on-error" .github/workflows/test.yml     # no longer on sweep-windows
grep -n -i "windows" .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml  # now referenced in the aggregate
```
then a real change pushed to `refs/for/main` earning `Verified +1` with the Windows job voting.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A passing `sweep (windows)` run on `main` while still advisory, with its run id recorded on this
   ticket.
2. The promotion is a separate later change that cites that run id.
3. `sweep (windows)` (or its reduced-subset successor) participates in the `Verified` vote.
4. `f850-674c-c89f-4b97` can be closed: its AC3 (epic with per-class children, `lock.py` first,
   each naming its proving command) and AC4 (`lock.py`'s unguarded `fcntl` fixed properly) are both
   satisfied by this epic, and AC5's invariant is intact.
data.title: S11: promote sweep (windows) into the Verified aggregate per ADR 0114 — the epic's exit criterion, LAST
